figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Identification of the STTR5 motif as a hallmark of HENases with high NTP substrate promiscuities.
(A) Synthesis of ADP- and CDP-heptoses by HBEs from varied kingdoms. CDP-heptose was only synthesized in the
cases of HldEMA, Cth-2, Be-6*, and Sa-4*. Be-6*: Be-6* (H692R); Sa-4*: Sa-4* (H652R). (B) Synthesis of UDP-
heptoses by HldCBP, Be-6*, and Sa-4*. All reactions were conducted with specific HENases combined with
appropriate HBEs listed in table S2. (C and D) present the docking results of ATP and CTP in the substrate binding
site of Cth-2, respectively. (E and F) present the MD simulation results of the nucleotidyltransferase domain of Be-6* with
CTP and UTP, respectively. The hydrogen bonds and cation-p interactions involved in (C to F) are indicated with
black dash lines and orange bold lines, respectively. (G) Verification of the STTR5 motif as a hallmark of the NTP substrate
promiscuities of HENases from diverse biological sources. HldEEC*: HldEEC* (C462R); HldCPB*: HldCPB* (H157R). The
column length represents the amount of NDP-heptose generated in each reaction. In (A, B, and G), HENases from
viruses, eukaryota, archaea, and bacteria are indicated in light brown, green, red, and blue, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Production of NDP-heptoses and the evolutionary relationship
of HENases and ALPK1s. (A) Synthesis of NDP-heptoses by different
HBE combinations at a simulated physiological condition (pH 7.2, S7P
0.1 mM, ATP 3.5 mM, CTP 0.3 mM, and UTP 0.7 mM). All data were
represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) (n = 3). (B) HPLC detection
of the cellular NDP-heptoses of two Burkholderia strains. (C) Tree of life
illustrating the widespread distribution of HENases across different kingdoms
